We need to propose a 5-step retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We need to produce JSON route with 5 reactions. Use templates from database. We have one template for TBS deprotection (template 29646) which goes from TBS-protected alcohol to free alcohol. That matches a step where we remove TBS protecting group. Our target currently has free OH groups? The SMILES shows O[C@H]1... there is a free OH at position 1, also an O attached to side chain O[C@@H]... that's an ether linking to side chain? Actually O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C is an O-alkyl linking to a side chain that contains a terminal CH2OH (CO). So there is a primary alcohol in side chain. The target also has a carboxylic acid at end (C(O)=O). So we need to think retrosynthetic steps: maybe start from simpler fragments: a cyclohexane core with two OH groups protected, then later deprotect. Also need to form the side chain via HWE (Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons) to install the conjugated diene and acid? Actually the side chain includes a conjugated diene with terminal COOH and a CH2OH substituent on the diene (C=C(CO)/C). That could be formed via Still-Gennari (Z-alkene) from an aldehyde and phosphonate. Also the carboxylic acid could be from oxidation of aldehyde after HWE? Or could be from a protected ester then hydrolyzed.

We need 5 steps. Let's outline plausible route:

Step 5 (final forward direction) is deprotection of TBS groups to give free OH. So retrosynthetic step: target -> precursor with TBS protected OHs.

Thus step 5 (retro) is removal of TBS: we need a precursor where the two OHs are protected as TBS ethers. Use template 29646 (reverse of protection). So precursor1: same skeleton but with OSi(tBu)(Me)2 groups at the two alcohol positions (the primary OH on side chain and the ring OH). Let's generate SMILES for protected version: Replace O- at start (ring OH) with O[TBS] i.e., O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C? Actually TBS is t-butyldimethylsilyl: Si(CH3)2C(CH3)3. SMILES: [Si](C)(C)(C(C)(C)C). So O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C. So protected SMILES: O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O? Wait the side chain also has OH (CH2OH) which may also be protected? The side chain OH is primary alcohol attached to the diene carbon. In target it's CH2OH (CO). That could be protected as TBS as well. The SMILES shows ...C=C(CO)/C meaning a carbon with substituent CO (i.e., CH2OH). So we need to protect that OH too. So three OH groups? Actually there is ring OH (at position 1), side chain ether O linking to side chain (that's an O attached to ring carbon, not OH), side chain primary alcohol (CH2OH). So only two OH groups: ring OH and side chain CH2OH. The ether O is not OH. So we need to protect both OHs with TBS.

Thus precursor after step 5: same skeleton but both OH replaced with OSi(TBS). We'll need to generate SMILES for that. Could be: O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O? Wait the side chain CH2OH also needs protection: the CH2OH becomes CH2O[Si](...). So the side chain part /C=C(CO)/C becomes /C=C(CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)/C. So final protected SMILES: O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. That's messy but okay.

Now step 4 (retro) could be formation of the carboxylic acid from an ester via hydrolysis (or from a protected ester). But we might incorporate that later.

Better to think forward: Starting from simple building blocks: a cyclohexanone maybe, then protect, then do HWE to attach side chain with diene and acid.

Let's search for HWE template (Still-Gennari) that forms C=C and carboxylic ester. Search for functional_groups_broken: ["C-C double bonds"] formed: ["carboxylic esters"]? Actually Still-Gennari forms double bond and carboxylic ester (the product is an alkene with ester). Our target has a carboxylic acid, not ester. Could be after HWE we have ester then hydrolyze to acid.

Search for template with broken: ["C-C double bonds"] formed: ["carboxylic esters"].
